RQ1: Demonstrates a general CubeSat mission/system model architecture using SysML and a CubeSat reference-model lineage.
Model combines architecture, requirements, behavior, parametric analyses, and external simulation for RAX mission energy/data behavior.
Does not establish modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge; it depends on STK/MATLAB analyses and mission/parameter data.
RQ2: Main supported outcomes are integrability/interoperability of tools, executable simulation, requirements traceability, and decision support for power/data trades.
Reliability/mission-assurance relevance is through simulation-based requirement checks and energy/data margins, not reliability prediction or flight evidence.
Reproducibility/reuse is planned via academic release, not demonstrated.
RQ3: Pre-physical requirements verification is integrated through SysML satisfy links and executable simulations for energy and data-download requirements.
No EPS verification procedures, verification matrix, formal test cases, SIL/HIL, or hardware test integration are presented.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Prototype not intended to be an accurate RAX satellite model.
Proof of concept limited to energy collection/management and data collection/management.
Detailed modeling of non-critical subsystems such as ADCS was minimized/excluded.
Trade studies are representative; combined parameter effects and more complex scheduling algorithms are future extensions.
Model/manual availability is planned for the academic community, not reported as completed.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No quantitative baseline comparison of MBSE versus document-centric or standalone-analysis process.
No independent validation, flight/operational data, or hardware integration/test evidence.
No formal EPS verification procedure/test artifact; verification is requirement checking through simulation.
No governance/ROI evidence and no model configuration/control process.
